paper_title: HotGauge: A Methodology for Characterizing Advanced Hotspots in Modern and Next Generation Processors

scenario.description: Case study of a high-performance client CPU similar to Intel Skylake with 7 cores, modeled across three process nodes (14nm, 10nm, 7nm) running SPEC2006 benchmarks. Single-threaded workloads executed at 5 GHz and 1.4 V (turbo boost condition) with 200M instruction ROI simulation. Transient thermal simulation with non-uniform temperature initialization modeling background OS tasks.
scenario.architecture: Out-of-order 7-core processor with SMT (2 threads/core), 224-entry ROB, 72-entry LQ, 56-entry SQ, 97-entry scheduler, private L1I/L1D (32KiB each), private L2 (512KiB), shared L3 (16MiB ring). Core aspect ratio 3×2. Floorplan inspired by Intel Skylake with functional units: Complex ALU, FP Instruction Window, Register Access Tables, Register Files, Reorder Buffer, misc core logic.
scenario.workload: SPEC2006 benchmarks (bzip2, gcc, omnetpp, povray, hmmer, gobmk, milc, namd, libquantum, gromacs, calculix, GemsFDTD). Single-threaded execution. Frequency 5 GHz, Voltage 1.4 V representing turbo boost.
scenario.operating_point: Maximum power operating point: 1.4 V, 5 GHz turbo boost. Thermal stack includes silicon IC (380 µm), solder TIM (200 µm), copper heat spreader (3000 µm), thermal grease (30 µm), HS483-ND heatsink with fan at 6000 rpm. Ambient 40°C, max junction 100°C (60°C thermal budget). Hotspot thresholds: Tth=80°C, MLTDth=25°C, radius=1mm.

original_setup.optimizer: McPAT v1.2 with novel modifications for 14nm/10nm/7nm scaling
original_setup.controller: No explicit controller; transient thermal simulation with non-uniform temperature initialization
original_setup.benchmark: SPEC2006 single-threaded workloads (bzip2, gcc, omnetpp, povray, hmmer, gobmk, milc, namd, libquantum, gromacs, calculix, GemsFDTD)

thermal_observable.location: On-die junction layer, hotspot definition threshold (Tth)
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak hotspot absolute temperature for hotspot detection; MLTD (Maximum Localized Temperature Difference) computed within 1mm radius

physical_mismatches.reason: 3D thermal stack (silicon IC, solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease, heatsink) models realistic cooling path; however, solder balls and motherboard excluded from model (noted in Fig. 4 caption). HotSniper (prior work) modeled only 45nm Gainestown with Hotspot-6.0; this work uses 3D-ICE for transient modeling of modern nodes.

Floorplan scaled uniformly across technology nodes (50% area reduction per node) with fixed core aspect ratio (3×2), but global wire delays do not scale proportionally. Paper acknowledges in Section III-E that die size historically remains constant as logic density increases, affecting critical timing path lengths.

Non-uniform temperature initialization implemented to model background OS tasks and recently context-switched workloads; however, exact thermal state of real hardware prior to ROI execution unknown and simulated only qualitatively.

Power model (McPAT v1.2) tuned using Cdyn validation against Intel Core i5 10310U (14nm mobile) and Core i7-1165G7 (10nm SuperFin) via Intel TAT. Validation error 11% (14nm) and 20% (10nm). 7nm model extrapolated; no real silicon validation available for 7nm case study.

Single-threaded SPEC2006 execution on single core; symmetric multi-threading (SMT) capability modeled (2 threads/core) but not exercised in primary results. Multi-threaded workload behavior and contention effects not characterized.

studio_assumptions: -Area scaling 50% per technology node (14nm→10nm→7nm) with constant floorplan layout and core placement
-Dynamic power (Cdyn) decreases 20% per technology node following transistor scaling trends
-Leakage power and area scaled to match advanced nodes using standard transistor scaling assumptions
-Frequency fixed at 5 GHz (turbo boost V-f point) and voltage at 1.4 V across all process nodes
-Heatsink model HS483-ND with fan at 6000 rpm remains identical across technology nodes; die area reduction increases thermal resistance Ψ per node
-Hotspot definition parameterized: Tth=80°C (max junction minus margin), MLTDth=25°C (timing slack), radius=1mm (global wire delay in clock cycle)
-Hotspot severity metric composed of three parameterized sigmoid functions calibrated from industry data: σdf (device failure at 115°C), σM and σT (timing margins with non-linear temperature effects)
-Background thermal state initialized with idle OS workload trace prior to ROI to model realistic multi-tasking environment
-Cache warm-up performed before 200M instruction ROI simulation; transient thermal dynamics captured with 1M cycle time steps
-Floorplan inspired by Intel Skylake; 50 functional units modeled compared to 6 units in prior HotSniper work
missing_inputs: No published floorplan geometry (x,y coordinates, widths, heights) for individual functional units beyond Fig. 5 schematic (7nm core floorplan visual only, no dimensions in mm)
Exact McPAT model parameter file (config XML) for Skylake proxy not provided; only high-level microarchitecture listed in Table I
Real hardware validation data for 7nm model unavailable; Cdyn validation limited to 14nm (i5-10310U) and 10nm (i7-1165G7). Extrapolation to 7nm unvalidated against silicon
Power trace ground truth: no actual measured power data from real Intel processors during SPEC2006 workload execution published; McPAT output used as proxy

Individual power dissipation per functional unit at each time step not explicitly reported in paper; power model output granularity stated as 'highest granularity setting' but exact breakdown not disclosed
Thermal model boundary condition validation: thermal grease and TIM interface with heatsink modeled, but actual contact resistance and uncertainties not quantified
Floorplan modifications for AVX512 mentioned (Section IV-D) as part of enhanced model additions but not detailed; baseline floorplan lacks explicit AVX unit in Table I or Fig. 5
Repository access verification: GitHub URL (https://github.com/TuftsCompArchLab/HotGauge) and Zenodo DOI (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5523504) cited but asset download/validation not performed
Exact version of Sniper pin tool, 3D-ICE library dependencies, and McPAT build configuration for reproducibility in appendix README reference only
SPEC2006 binary compilation flags, workload input datasets, and region-of-interest (ROI) demarcation markers not specified; only 200M instruction window and cache warm-up mentioned
